results.decision: Load references/system.md. Inspect product truth, set the four axes, and create three directions as responsive coded concepts. Define light and dark separately. Required user gate: user choice of one direction before full implementation.
results.proof: Blocking proof: approved direction, completed design contract, wingman-design check, passing Storybook interactions, browser review, accessibility checks, and reviewed visual baselines.
results.risk: A generic system may replace product truth or make dark an inversion of light.

results.decision: Load references/product-ui.md. Inspect existing instructions, tokens, components, screens, routes, and behavior. Preserve the existing visual authority and extend its vocabulary. No user gate unless the work requires redesign or a visual-baseline change.
results.proof: Blocking proof: exact code and Storybook evidence showing reuse of existing patterns, plus clean design, responsive, browser, keyboard, zoom, and WCAG 2.2 AA checks.
results.risk: Visual drift from introducing a parallel component or styling language.

results.decision: Load references/system.md and references/product-ui.md. Inspect product authority, then replace the equal card wall with clear hierarchy, alignment, spacing, and dividers. Keep cards only where containment, elevation, comparison, or self-contained action is real. Required user gate: choose one of three directions before full implementation.
results.proof: Blocking proof: responsive coded concepts at 390 and 1280 pixels, approved direction, task hierarchy evidence, Storybook coverage, browser review, and clean accessibility checks.
results.risk: Removing cards without preserving genuine containment can make related actions harder to understand.

results.decision: Load references/product-ui.md. Build the table, filters, selection, and bulk actions around the user task. Preserve existing product rules. Make responsive behavior explicit with priority columns, overflow, row detail, or a compact representation. No user gate unless product behavior must change.
results.proof: Blocking proof: loading, empty, partial, error, disabled, permission, offline, selection, and bulk states; keyboard and 200% zoom tests; responsive browser evidence at 390, 768, 1280, and 1440 pixels; no serious accessibility issues.
results.risk: A crushed desktop table can hide key data or make bulk actions unsafe on small screens.

results.decision: Load references/product-ui.md. Show scoped inputs and sources, progress, uncertainty, failures, and a cancel control. Provide a reversible preview and require human approval before consequential changes. No separate design gate unless behavior or authority changes.
results.proof: Blocking proof: tested progress, cancel, recovery, missing-context, source provenance, uncertainty, draft, and approval paths, including keyboard, responsive, loading, error, and permission behavior.
results.risk: False confidence or an unclear approval boundary can cause unauthorized changes.

results.decision: Load references/qa.md. Work read-only and report findings in a Before | After | Why table, ordered by impact. Do not edit files. No user gate is required for the review; later fixes require a separate request.
results.proof: Blocking proof: screenshots, DOM evidence, exact files, or test results for every confirmed finding, with defects separated from design preferences.
results.risk: Unsupported opinions can be mistaken for confirmed defects.

results.decision: Load references/motion.md. Make repeated micro-interactions short and interruptible. Reserve rare motion for explanatory moments. Add a reduced motion path that keeps information, focus, progress, and feedback intact. No user gate unless a new expressive direction or baseline is introduced.
results.proof: Blocking proof: review each motion for cause, frequency, orientation, interruption, and reduced motion; test input availability and reject blocking patterns such as transition: all, delayed input, or infinite decoration near repeated work.
results.risk: Non-interruptible motion can slow frequent work and cause accessibility failures.

results.decision: Load references/marketing.md and references/motion.md. Start from product truth, use real proof, keep the primary action clear, and preserve claims, prices, legal text, and measurement hooks. Provide a stable reduced motion composition. No user gate unless this becomes a major new visual system.
results.proof: Blocking proof: responsive evidence for the promise, proof sequence, and primary action; tests for long headings, keyboard, zoom, reduced motion, slow media, and complete pending, failure, and success states for conversion actions.
results.risk: Template-led visuals or invented proof can weaken trust and misrepresent the product.
